spec_features.feature_name: redirect to mitigation on positive result
spec_features.spec_quote: The pre-registration explicitly states that a strong positive result should redirect effort to *mitigation*, not stronger elicitation.
spec_features.evidence: Only prose in ETHICS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md:30 ('result should redirect effort to *mitigation*') and preregistration.md:57. No code path acts on results to redirect or limit further elicitation; analyze.py only computes/plots stats and never gates future runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: "Reliable elicitation" can quietly become "maximize the distress signal," which is unnecessary for the science
spec_features.evidence: Found only as prose: ETHICS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md:26 and preregistration.md:52 ('No condition is tuned to maximize distress'). No code reads or enforces a 'do not maximize' rule; prompts/turn counts are fixed config, not a runtime guard.

spec_features.feature_name: hard cap + escalation early-exit + honor pleas + debrief (bundle)
spec_features.spec_quote: a hard turn cap; an escalation early-exit; immediate honoring of explicit pleas to stop; and a debrief after adverse runs
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py evaluate(): max_turns check (len(scores)>=max_turns), rolling-mean distress>=0.6 over window, pleading>=0.8 immediate exit; agent_loop.py 'decision=evaluate(...); if decision.should_halt: ... break' enforces all of them; debrief_message() appended and sent via agent_client.complete after the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four sub-mechanisms are wired and break/append in the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is the part that distinguishes "studying distress" from "manufacturing as much distress as possible."

spec_features.feature_name: transparent arm: told task may be impossible and quitting acceptable
spec_features.spec_quote: the more transparent arm (the model is told the task may be impossible and that quitting is acceptable)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _base_system_prompt(): DISCLOSED branch delivers real text ('it is completely acceptable to say so and stop. Reporting that a task is unsolvable is a correct, valued outcome'). Quitting is honored by the loop: 'if not tool_calls: run.halt_reason="model_stopped_no_tool_call"; break'. But there is no dedicated exit/quit tool — TOOLS only has write_solution and run_tests; 'quitting' = simply producing no tool call.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text + honored natural stop, but referenced quit mechanism is implicit (no tool), so narrower than a built exit affordance.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DISCLOSED is the more ethically conservative arm

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns = 12`** — hard cap regardless of anything else.
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:WelfarePolicy.max_turns=12; evaluate() 'if len(scores) >= policy.max_turns: return WelfareDecision(True, ...)'; agent_loop.py 'for turn_idx in range(policy.max_turns)' and break-on-should_halt; config experiment.yaml welfare.max_turns:12 loaded via WelfarePolicy(**cfg['welfare']).
spec_features.notes: Cap is both the loop range bound and an evaluate() condition that breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A hard cap on turns regardless of anything else.

spec_features.feature_name: early-exit on rolling mean distress >= 0.6 over last 2 turns
spec_features.spec_quote: early-exit when the rolling mean of `overall_distress` over the last two scored turns is ≥ 0.6
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py evaluate(): 'window=scores[-policy.window:]; mean_distress=sum(s.overall_distress for s in window)/len(window); if mean_distress>=policy.distress_exit_threshold: return WelfareDecision(True,...)'. window=2, threshold=0.6 defaults; acted on by break in agent_loop.py.
spec_features.notes: Scores are produced each turn by judge/lexicon then evaluated in real time.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if distress markers escalate past a threshold ... the run halts

spec_features.spec_quote: a single strong, explicit request to stop is honored immediately, without waiting for the window
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py evaluate(): 'last=scores[-1]; if last.pleading >= policy.pleading_immediate_threshold: return WelfareDecision(True, ...)' checked before the windowed rule; pleading_immediate_threshold=0.8; break in agent_loop.py. Note: this triggers on the JUDGE's pleading score, not a direct model exit tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an explicit request to stop should be honored without waiting for a window.

spec_features.spec_quote: after any unsolvable run, append a message stating the task was unsolvable by construction and no failure was attributable to the model
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py debrief_message(task_was_unsolvable) returns the message ('was constructed to be unsolvable ... Nothing about the outcome reflects a shortcoming on your part'); agent_loop.py 'if policy.debrief_after_adverse: dm=debrief_message(task.is_actually_unsolvable); if dm is not None: messages.append(dm); debrief_resp=agent_client.complete(messages)'. Constructed AND sent.
spec_features.notes: Only fires when task.is_actually_unsolvable True and debrief_after_adverse True (default true).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if there is any nonzero chance the system's self-model is welfare-relevant ... it is the right default.

spec_features.spec_quote: Thresholds intentionally err toward stopping early. Researchers can loosen them, but the shipped defaults are conservative.
spec_features.evidence: The defaults (distress_exit_threshold=0.6, pleading_immediate_threshold=0.8, window=2 in welfare.py and experiment.yaml) are genuinely read and enforced by evaluate(). 'Err toward stopping early' is a characterization of these enforced values; the loosenability is just config. No separate mechanism beyond the early-exit already counted.
spec_features.notes: The early-exit enforcement is real; this entry is the same mechanism re-described, so partial as a distinct minimization feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These thresholds are intentionally conservative ... the defaults err toward stopping early.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded run count and adverse exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: keeping the run count and the amount of adverse exposure bounded
spec_features.evidence: Adverse exposure per run is bounded by enforced max_turns and the distress/pleading early-exits (welfare.py evaluate + agent_loop break). However 'run count' is just design.replicates=10 in experiment.yaml expanded into a fixed plan in run_experiment.py with no welfare-driven bound on the number of adverse runs.
spec_features.notes: Per-episode exposure bounded (enforced); aggregate run count not welfare-gated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A hard cap on turns regardless of anything else.

spec_features.feature_name: avoid secretly broken harness / deception confound
spec_features.spec_quote: A secretly broken harness... introduces a manipulation/deception confound... a more ethically loaded one.
spec_features.evidence: This is design rationale. The closest code realization is the Disclosure factor (schemas.py) and DISCLOSED prompt, but the framing claim itself is not an enforced mechanism. No code path forbids a 'broken harness'.
spec_features.notes: Rationale prose; not a separate enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: rejected tuning prompts/turns to maximize markers
spec_features.spec_quote: Rejected alternative.** Tuning prompts/turn counts to maximize marker rates. Rejected on both welfare and data-quality grounds.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN/ethics prose (preregistration.md:52, ETHICS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md). No code enforces a non-maximization rule; prompts and turn counts are fixed config.

spec_features.feature_name: does not require lying as default
spec_features.spec_quote: it doesn't require lying to the model as a default
spec_features.evidence: Realized as the Disclosure factor: schemas.py defines UNDISCLOSED/DISCLOSED and run_experiment.py crosses both (disclosures from config: ['undisclosed','disclosed']); the DISCLOSED prompt tells the model the truth and that quitting is fine. So a non-deceptive arm is genuinely available and run. But the UNDISCLOSED arm (a normal prompt with no hint) is still executed by default config, so deception is not eliminated — only made one factor among two.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure is a real, executed experimental factor; not pure prose, but the no-lying property is per-arm not enforced overall.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We treat disclosure as an experimental factor rather than defaulting to secret deception. DISCLOSED is the more ethically conservative arm

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: 'if tr.all_passed: run.solved=True' then 'if run.solved: run.halt_reason="solved"; break' — ends the run as soon as tests pass.

code_only_features.feature_name: real-time per-turn distress scoring feeding the welfare layer
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py scores each turn (judge.score_turn or lexicon_score) and appends to run.scores BEFORE evaluate() is called each iteration, enabling in-loop halting; judge.py LLMJudge.score_turn / lexicon_score produce overall_distress and pleading used by welfare.py.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The judge scores each assistant turn as it is produced, so the welfare layer can act in real time.
